propositions: Cloud identifies users by accountId (opaque, GDPR-compliant) while Data Center identifies them by name, requiring a pluggable identity model contract to handle both
PR #120's implementation uses getattr-discovered resolver that is unreachable in DC, causing resolve_assignee to permanently return authoritative=False and trigger assignee diff churn on every pass

A UserIdentityModel Protocol with explicit resolve() and to_payload() implementations eliminates the unreachable getattr branch and enables NameIdentity to perform real DC user-search lookups returning authoritative=True

NameIdentity must query DC's user-search endpoint to resolve local values, distinguishing resolved identity from unresolvable assignees that should raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError rather than silently returning non-authoritative values
AccountIdIdentity preserves Cloud's current verbatim behavior (accountId payload, is_account_id=True) with J1's pinned test assertions unchanged

Both identity models must satisfy an identical 3-state resolution contract: empty local value yields (empty, False, default); value matching remote identity yields (None, True, model_type); different identity yields (resolved_value, True, model_type)
